overview: Baker Hughes is a global energy and industrial technology company that provides equipment, technology, and services across the full energy value chain, from oil and gas well construction and production to gas turbines, compression, and industrial power systems. The company operates through two primary reporting segments -- Oilfield Services & Equipment (OFSE) and Industrial & Energy Technology (IET) -- and completed the $13.6 billion acquisition of Chart Industries in July 2026, which will be reported as a third segment focused on cryogenic and thermal management equipment. Baker Hughes operates in more than 120 countries, with a customer base spanning national and international oil companies, LNG developers, industrial manufacturers, utilities, and increasingly data center/power infrastructure developers.

business_model.summary: Roughly half of revenue comes from OFSE (oilfield services and equipment tied to drilling, completions, production, and subsea for oil and gas customers) and roughly half from IET (gas technology equipment/turbomachinery, industrial technology, and new energy/climate solutions), with the newly closed Chart Industries acquisition adding a third segment focused on cryogenic and thermal-management equipment for LNG, industrial gas, and hydrogen. IET is increasingly an equipment-plus-long-cycle-services model with large multi-year order backlogs and growing recurring aftermarket/service revenue, while OFSE is more transactional and tied to near-term drilling/completion activity.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - national and international oil companies, LNG developers/operators, industrial and power generation customers, data center/power infrastructure developers, and utilities
business_model.geographic_mix: Global operations across North America, Middle East, Asia Pacific, Europe, Latin America, and Africa; Middle East and Asia are central to growth strategy, with meaningful exposure to Saudi Aramco and other Gulf national oil companies

competitive_position.market_position: Second-largest oilfield services company by revenue (behind SLB, generating roughly 77% of SLB's revenue) in the 'Big Three' OFS oligopoly with SLB and Halliburton; holds a dominant, near-monopoly position (~90% share) in turbomachinery for LNG liquefaction via its GE-heritage Frame 7/Frame 9 turbines and related equipment

moat_factors.description: Near-90% share of large-scale LNG liquefaction turbomachinery; Frame 7/Frame 9 turbines are the de facto industry standard, creating high switching costs and long-cycle aftermarket service revenue
Large global installed base of equipment (subsea trees, turbomachinery, compression) generates recurring, high-margin services and parts revenue over decades-long equipment life
GE heritage gives deep rotating equipment and turbomachinery engineering expertise; complementary to newly acquired Chart Industries' cryogenic/thermal management IP

moat_factors.factor: Diversified portfolio vs. pure-play OFS peers
moat_factors.description: IET segment provides exposure to LNG, power generation, data centers, and new energy that SLB and Halliburton largely lack, reducing pure oil-price cyclicality
Operations in 120+ countries support large, complex international and offshore projects that smaller competitors cannot service

weaknesses: OFSE remains exposed to oil price cycles and NOC/IOC capex discipline, including recently signaled pressure on Saudi Aramco spending
Competes with Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries in turbomachinery, which have won LNG contracts in 2024-2025
Integration risk from the large, recently closed Chart Industries acquisition ($13.6B, third-largest in company history)
OFSE segment margins remain lower and more volatile than IET margins
Historically complex, GE-spinout capital structure required years of portfolio simplification

growth_drivers: LNG buildout: continued global liquefaction capacity additions favor Baker Hughes' dominant turbomachinery position
AI data center power demand: gas turbine orders (NovaLT, Frame 5, Frame 6/7) for modular 150-300MW power blocks; data center Power Systems orders reached $1B in Q1 2026 alone, matching all of 2025
New Energy portfolio (hydrogen, CCUS, geothermal, emissions management, electrification): revenue grew from a few hundred million in 2022 to over $2B in 2025, guided to $2.4-2.6B in 2026

Chart Industries acquisition: expands addressable market to more than $400B, adds cryogenic/thermal management and recurring aftermarket revenue, targeting $325M in annualized cost synergies by year three
Record IET order backlog: Q2 2026 IET bookings doubled year-over-year to $7.1B with backlog up 19% to an all-time high; Horizon 2 (2026-2028) IET order outlook raised to more than $45B

Portfolio simplification/capital discipline: divestitures (Precision Sensors & Instrumentation to Crane for $1.15B, surface pressure control JV) redeploying capital toward higher-margin, higher-growth technology businesses
International and offshore OFSE project pipeline, including FPSO awards and subsea/gas infrastructure

business.description: OFSE demand is directly tied to customer E&P spending, which fluctuates with oil and gas prices
Pressure on Saudi Aramco and other national oil company capital budgets has delayed some projects
Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries are increasingly winning LNG and turbine contracts, eroding BKR's historical dominance over time
IET revenue recognition lags bookings by multiple years, making near-term results sensitive to project timing and cancellations

financial.description: The $13.6B all-cash-and-stock deal increases debt load and requires successful integration to achieve targeted synergies
Significant international revenue creates exposure to currency fluctuations in emerging markets
Large equipment and project-based businesses require substantial working capital management

regulatory.description: Evolving emissions regulations affect both traditional oilfield operations and new energy investment economics (CCUS, hydrogen incentives)
Operations in Russia, Middle East, and other geopolitically sensitive regions expose the company to sanctions risk and compliance costs
Large acquisitions like Chart Industries face regulatory review, though this deal has closed

macro.description: Middle East conflicts (including risks to the Strait of Hormuz), Russia-Ukraine war, and other conflicts create supply chain, demand, and safety risks; management has described geopolitical risk as elevated
A recession would reduce energy demand and industrial capex, pressuring both OFSE and IET order flow
Higher rates raise financing costs for capital-intensive customer projects (LNG trains, power plants) and for BKR's own acquisition financing
Slower-than-expected new energy adoption or policy reversals (e.g., reduced government support for hydrogen/CCUS) could dampen New Energy segment growth

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Management describes an 'energy demand decade' driven by rising global energy consumption, LNG capacity expansion, AI/data center power needs, and continued oil and gas infrastructure investment alongside growing low-carbon/CCUS spend
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate to high for OFSE (tied to oil/gas capex cycles); more moderate for IET given long-cycle LNG/power projects and growing recurring services revenue, providing some counter-cyclical balance
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - large customer capital projects (LNG, power, data centers) and BKR's own debt load (increased post-Chart acquisition) are sensitive to financing costs

recent_developments.event: Completed $13.6 billion acquisition of Chart Industries, adding cryogenic and thermal management capabilities as a new third operating segment; targeting $325M in annualized cost synergies by year three

Reported record quarterly results: adjusted EPS of $0.64 (vs. $0.49 expected), revenue of $6.74B; IET bookings doubled year-over-year to $7.1B with backlog up 19% to an all-time high; raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $27.35B and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $4.85B
Booked $1 billion in data center-related Power Systems orders in a single quarter, matching the entirety of 2025; record IET bookings drove margin expansion
Closed $1.15 billion sale of Precision Sensors & Instrumentation (Druck, Panametrics, Reuter-Stokes brands) product line to Crane Company, continuing portfolio simplification
Reported record full-year IET bookings and full-year 2025 results; IET revenue grew 10% to $13.41B (48% of total revenue) with segment EBITDA up 21% to $2.48B
Announced agreement to acquire Chart Industries for $210/share (~$13.6B enterprise value), positioned as accelerating the Energy & Industrial Technology strategy

Stock trading near $57, up roughly 40%+ year-to-date in 2026, driven by data center/AI power demand narrative and Chart deal synergy expectations; 21 analysts hold a consensus 'Moderate Buy' with average price target of $71.81 (~25% upside)

items.notes: Raised following record Q2 2026 results and the completed Chart Industries acquisition contribution
Reflects margin expansion in both OFSE and IET plus incremental Chart contribution
Raised on record bookings momentum in LNG, power systems, and data center-related orders
Multi-year cumulative order outlook raised on sustained LNG, gas infrastructure, and power systems demand
Up from over $2 billion in 2025; includes CCUS, hydrogen, geothermal, and emissions management
Cost synergy target set at deal announcement; commercial synergies cited as additional upside not yet quantified
Guidance assumes Middle East activity levels remain broadly stable through year-end, with a modest revenue drag from regional disruptions

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Lorenzo Simonelli has characterized the current environment as an 'energy demand decade,' citing rising global energy consumption, infrastructure investment across oil, gas and power, growth in CCUS/low-carbon projects, and AI/data center power requirements as durable tailwinds. Management highlighted record IET bookings and backlog, robust free cash flow ($1.1B in Q2 2026), and continued portfolio discipline (Precision Sensors divestiture, surface pressure control JV) alongside integration of the newly closed Chart Industries acquisition as the primary near-term execution priorities.

bull_case: Near-monopoly position in LNG turbomachinery (~90% share) positions Baker Hughes to capture a multi-year global LNG capacity build-out
AI data center power demand is a new, fast-growing order stream (gas turbines/power systems) that is largely uncorrelated with oil prices
Chart Industries acquisition expands the addressable market to over $400B and adds recurring cryogenic/thermal aftermarket revenue with $325M in identified cost synergies
IET's growing mix (48%+ of revenue, record backlog) reduces reliance on cyclical OFSE and supports margin expansion and more resilient, recurring services revenue
New Energy revenue (hydrogen, CCUS, geothermal) has scaled from a few hundred million to a multi-billion dollar run rate, providing a long-duration option on the energy transition
bear_case: OFSE remains exposed to oil price volatility and NOC capex discipline, including signaled pressure on Saudi Aramco spending
Integration risk on the large, recently closed $13.6B Chart Industries deal could distract management and delay promised synergies
Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries are increasingly winning LNG/turbomachinery contracts, threatening BKR's historically dominant market share over time
Stock has already re-rated meaningfully (up 40%+ YTD in 2026) on the AI/data center narrative, raising the bar for continued upside and leaving less room for execution missteps
Elevated geopolitical risk (Middle East conflict, Strait of Hormuz exposure, Russia-Ukraine) could disrupt operations, supply chains, or customer capex decisions
